name: Slide Commit
description: A button whose handle you must drag all the way to confirm; the result is shown with a spinner and then a success or rejection chip.
interactionNotes: Drag the handle to the side. If you pull too little, it springs back and hits the home wall; if you reach the end, it confirms. With the keyboard: the right or up arrow moves forward (a tenth of the track per press) and `End` confirms directly; the left or down arrow moves back, and `Home` or `Escape` returns it to the start.

props.name: label
props.description: The text in the middle of the chip; it clears as you drag.

props.name: doneLabel
props.description: The text next to the check mark after confirmation.

props.name: errorLabel
props.description: Replaces the hint text, in the danger color, after a rejection.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Called when the handle reaches the end. If it returns a Promise, a spinner is shown.

props.name: onDone
props.description: Called when the completed chip opens.

props.name: onError
props.description: Called with the rejection reason; otherwise the component swallows it.

props.name: trackColor
props.description: The track behind the handle.

props.name: handleColor
props.description: The handle and the fill it drags; its arrow color is chosen for legibility over it.

props.name: successColor
props.description: The fill of the completed chip.

props.name: dangerColor
props.description: The handle and error text color after a rejection.

props.name: width
props.description: Track width; the travel distance scales with it.

props.name: height
props.description: Track height; the handle is 8 pixels smaller.

props.name: radius
props.description: Track corner radius; the handle corner is 4 pixels smaller so they stay concentric.

props.name: speed
props.description: Speed of opening and returning after release.

props.name: returnBounce
props.description: The energy left when returning to the home wall; zero means it stops immediately.

props.name: landingDip
props.description: How much the track dips when the completed chip lands; zero turns it off.

props.name: holdMs
props.description: How long the completed chip stays before it collapses; zero means it stays until remount.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims it and ignores input.

props.name: autoPreview
props.description: Site preview only: it drags the handle to the end with animation and releases it; the rubber stretch and the spring return follow the real path.

props.name: icon
props.description: Replaces the arrow inside the handle.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class for the root element.

tips: If `onConfirm` returns a Promise, a spinner is shown — that's the right way to wire it to the network. If it fails, the handle shakes and returns, so the user knows it didn't work without your page showing a separate message.
The spinner deliberately stays for at least 300 milliseconds. Without that, a fast response would make it skip a frame and vanish, and the user would never see "in progress".
Labels are UI, not data — they are shown on the chip itself, exposed as `aria-label` and announced in the live region. So keep them Persian; only change them if you supply your own label.

Unlike most right-to-left components, **nothing here mirrors and nothing should**: all the geometry is physical and the arrow points the same way the handle moves. So the right key means "forward", exactly like the drag direction.
`holdMs={0}` keeps the completed chip until the component remounts — for when you show the result somewhere else.
